title: Research on the Parametric Design and Application of Ceramic Modeling Based on Python
content: In response to the growing diverse needs of the ceramic industry, this paper creatively employs the ErgoLAB Human-Machine Environment Synchronization Platform to collect eye movement, gaze trajectory, dwell time, and various modalities of data including electroencephalographic and skin conductance data, thereby identifying the core parameters for parametric design. On this basis, a parametric design process for ceramic shapes based on Python programming language has been developed, covering key stages such as parameter selection, shape generation, and model visualization, and a model library containing multiple classic ceramic shapes has been rapidly constructed. By introducing physiological human-machine testing and ergonomics experiments, the intrinsic mechanisms of ceramic shape parametric design have been thoroughly investigated. To optimize the design, a fuzzy comprehensive evaluation was used to conduct qualitative analysis of the parametric models, generating a series of aesthceramic modelingetically pleasing new shapes. Combined with ceramic 3D printing technology, a complete closed loop from design to manufacturing has been achieved, verifying the manufacturability of the designs and demonstrating the significant potential of parametric design in advancing the ceramic manufacturing industry towards intelligence, personalization, and diversification. This study not only deepens the understanding of ceramic shape parametric design but also provides strong support for the diverse development of the ceramic industry, while offering valuable references for parametric design in other industrial design fields.
